steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: A disaster! This is a disaster, I tell you!

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: You call this interior design? No wonder no one hires Siestans for design work. This is a tourist destination, yet it has no architectural style of its own, and you don't even know how to copy someone else's properly!

spans.text: interior design? No wonder no one hires Siestans for design work. This is a tourist destination, yet it has no architectural style of its own, and you don't even know how to copy someone else's properly!

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: How could you sully the elegance of Victorian style like this? Look at this table. I said I wanted it to have a marble-like texture. Instead, you went with this cheap, low quality wood!

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: Perhaps you should look at your budget and again see if you gave me enough for even half a slab of faux marble.

spans.text: Perhaps you should look at your budget and again see if you gave me enough for even

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Hah! Alright. Looks like you don't quite understand your place, Miss Ann-Maier.

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: If it wasn't for me, you'd still be following the Sargonian caravans, fumbling your way around town! There's nothing stopping me from reporting you to the cops as an undocumented immigrant who illegally entered Columbia. Then, you won't see so much as a dime!

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: If you do that, I'll report you for sheltering and hiring an illegal immigrant! Now pay me!

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Why... you!

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Hmph, what a foolish Siestan. So crude and disrespectful...

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: When the city's so stupid as to willingly gave up their obsidian mining industry, their bread and butter, there are bound to be citizens like you with no respect for others!

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: (Money first... Yell at him only after you get the money...)

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Nothing to say? The tragic thing about you is that you haven't even realized Siesta's foolishness, and you're here shouting and accusing me!

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: (I can't make nothing from this job. I need my traveling money...)

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: If you people had chosen to join Victoria all those years ago, you would long have become citizens of the empire, indulged in the opulence the empire has to offer, and found your place in the empire's grand history! Instead, you're here, trying to earn a bit of coin to get on your way...

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Hmph, looks like you're at least savvy enough to understand my point.

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Take this. It's your pay. Hmph, count it well. It's in Victorian pounds. You know the denominations, right? Don't you even think I'm trying to shortchange you, lest you make yourself seem ill-mannered.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: Mister, you aren't deserving of my manners.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: You don't know anything about Siesta's history. You don't even know the first thing about the Victorian architectural history you're so proud of. What's more, Victoria's glory is all thanks to your ancestors' contributions. It hasn't got one bit to do with you.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: Why don't you go take a look at the buildings in Victoria and see how Siesta's obsidian has changed your architectural style and become the kind of luxury commodity that you snobs adore so much?

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: Who's the one with a narrow perspective here?

steps.name: Bankrupt Merchant
steps.text: Why you...!

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: The Siestans closed off the mines to protect the environment. Everything we do, we do it for the sake of our homeland's future. Not like some stingy man who's just talking about the glorious past over and over to win himself respect.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: I'm going back to rebuild my homeland and help breathe new life into it, but what about you? What have you done for Victoria given the shape it's in these days?
Ann-Maier curls her lips a little, and measures the thickness of the stack of bills with her hand.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: Even the Columbian demolition crews pay more, oh noble employer.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: I only hope your tastes will help you make your comeback.

steps.name: Impoverished Girl
steps.text: Now cheerio!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Need to go over anything again? It doesn't hurt to be careful.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Everything of value is still here, and the house is in one piece. That's good enough for me.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I'll send you the reward I promised you. The exhibition-grade obsidian and the certificate will make it to you in probably two months.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: That's great!

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: I'm looking forward to it.
The collector's eyes briefly lights up, though his excitement doesn't last particularly long.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Is there some kind of bewitching power to these obsidians that has you enthralled like this?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Are you interested in obsidian yourself? I suppose not... I've learned my lesson. There are very few people out there who truly have an eye for their beauty. Most with have their eyes on obsidians are up to no good!

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Never mind. I shan't bother you any longer! Goodbye!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Mr. Pelipper Brown. Are you perhaps related to the bankrupt Siestan tycoon, Beat Brown?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Don't even mention that scary old man...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: There may not be many who still remember him, but I'm sure he was much more well known back when obsidian was still Siesta's main export.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I spotted this name while I was going over the data. I didn't expect his successor to be running a little hot spring hotel in the area.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: The volcano gave Siesta plenty of riches, and the hot springs are no less wonderful than the obsidian.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: The old man died a couple years ago. Oripathy.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: He never went anywhere close to the mines, but he got infected on his way to Columbia for vacation when the car's Originium engine broke down.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Oh... I'm sorry to hear...

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: He wasn't really a good man, but his mines did create many jobs. If his protective measures were just a little more comprehensive, perhaps he would've won the gratitude of the miners.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I've heard that when the government announced the ban on obsidian mining, your mines were the first ones to work toward shutting down.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: What else was I supposed to do? The only alternative I had was to break the law.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Alright, Mr. Brown. I hope we'll get to work together again in the future. Your hot spring hotel is very spectacular. Would you perhaps be interested in developing it into a hot spring resort?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: I'll pass. I'd rather not go through all the ruckus—That is, unless you make me an offer that I truly can't refuse. Say, an even bigger obsidian that's even more pleasing to the eye.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Speaking of which... your obsidian collection here have all been delicately cut and polished. How come there's a geode that hasn't been polished whatsoever?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Oh... Don't you get any funny ideas about it.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: That thing's more expensive than all the pieces in the hotel combined.
Adele.
...Adele?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Is this... Mutti's hand?)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (So warm...)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Mutti... is stroking my shoulder...)
Wake up, Adele.
Adele, you mustn't sleep here. You'll catch a cold.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (I won't...)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (It's very warm... when you're here by my side.)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mutti...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele?
Keller hides the surprised expression on her face and reaches her hand out to gently pat Adele's head.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Are you awake?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh... Professor Keller.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Did I just...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm sorry, Professor Keller! I fell asleep...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: You seem exhausted.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Did you have a nightmare? Are you feeling unwell?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Or is it your illness...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm okay...
Adele sees that the elder scholar is looking at her with a worried expression. Her eyes are full of concern. During their short time together, she has never seen the stern scholar look so gentle.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller... Could you tell me just...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Just what happened at Wilhelm University all those years ago...?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I don't understand, Adele. What are you asking?

steps.name: Gentle Creature
steps.text: No, Adele. We have to go.

steps.name: Solemn Creature
steps.text: Yes. It's time.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Where are you going?

steps.name: Gentle Creature
steps.text: We have to head back up the volcano before it starts to rain.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Rain...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller... Does the word 'rain' have any other meaning?
Silence.
Keller bites her lip, as though there is something that she wants to say, but she nonetheless swallows those words back down.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele... When this observation is over, I will tell you everything, alright?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly, you told me before that every Little Black Sheep is different. They... aren't just your clones, right...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Are those dreams... really just dreams?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: We've found the 'Northern Wind' and the 'Seed.' Will you give me all these answers if we find the 'Fur?'

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Why does it seem like... everyone is hiding just about everything from me...?
There is no answer.
And unlike the mischievous kind of silence she got before, Adele can feel that something has truly disappeared from her side.
Adele looks around the empty exhibit hall, and finds the whistling rock specimen that was lost and then recovered a few days ago sitting where it has sat, having not moved an inch.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly?

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Good morning, Siesta. Today is August 21, 1099.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The humidity is 63%, visibility 12km, wind's blowing south-southwest. Estimated three days until volcanic eruption...

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The exciting time is almost upon us. How is everyone feeling? Who do you want to share the moment with?

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Did any of you forget anything back in Old Siesta? If you did—that's too bad. I mean, what's anyone supposed to do? You only have yourself to blame for being so careless in your move. It's all too late now!

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: But whatever the case may be, we should try to look at the bright side. It's only by casting away our old burdens that we can better welcome the future.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: 'You Go Your Way!'

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Let's get our day started with this song from the Reef Band.

steps.name: Busy Voice
steps.text: Watch out, be careful. Hold that sign up. It's a bit heavy, so get a good grip.

steps.name: Exhausted Voice
steps.text: It's such an old sign. Since we're tearing things down anyway, can't we cut it up first before we take it down?

steps.name: Busy Voice
steps.text: Yeah, we may be tearing the place down and moving, but if Old Man Mockingbird were to find out about you cutting his sign down with an axe, he'd climb out of his grave and beat the living hell out of you.

steps.name: Busy Voice
steps.text: Stop complaining. 3—2—

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Mister, are all these instruments here discounted?

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Yeah, they're all as cheap as they get.

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I couldn't bring myself to, but I figured I wouldn't have a chance to sell them once I move to the city center. Keeping the instruments on gag order? Now that would be a real waste.

spans.text: I couldn't bring myself to, but I figured I wouldn't have a chance to sell them once I move to the city center. Keeping the instruments on gag order? Now

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: How about it? Why don't you pick one? I remember you said you've always wanted your own guitar. I could give you a free textbook on how to play, too.

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: This discounted guitar... goes for a hundred and fifty certs... Enis says he earns three for every hour he works...

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: L-Let me think about it...

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Not like we can bring it with us. Might as well take it out and let everyone have some fun.

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: We want to do something special that we can look back on before we all move out of this street.

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Like what? Drink? Look at the sea? Set off some fireworks?

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: We'll invite all the old miners that we used to drink with and the other shopkeepers on the street, have them bring their friends and family—

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: How about we have a party at the empty plate the night before the eruption? A container party. Sounds cool, doesn't it?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Mr. Costa.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Oh, the punk from White Volcano. What are you doing here? Don't you need to look after the shop?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: We're preparing for our move, too.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: We don't have a lot of customers these days... If I don't come out to earn some cash, we all might just go hungry.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I'm sorry about Grandpa Mockingbird... May he rest in peace.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: He was getting on in years. It was going to happen...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Perhaps he's in some other place, sharing his taste in coffee.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: No need to be so polite. Just a couple years ago, you were still a punk who would come out to watch my concerts at night instead of going to bed. Just call me Costa like before.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: If I remember correctly, it was the 'Corybantic Costa.'

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm not so corybantic anymore. My guitar, bass, synth... Sold them all long ago.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Truth be told, I really miss sneaking into the venues with the adults, too. Those were the good times.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You'll get it once you get a little older. There are no such things as good times.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: All times are a waste of time. It's only after we waste our time away that we can bring our memories back out, dust them off, and think back on how great those times were.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Thinking back... I must've pissed Grandpa off so much back then.
The city hall staffer squints at the cars on the street. The cars zoom past them, leaving behind a few streaks of silhouette in his vision.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: So, Enis, if there's anything you want to do, do it now. Don't wait till everything you knew no longer resembled what they once were. By then, it's all too late.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Yeah... I will.
Costa taps Enis's shoulder and sighs.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: The residents of the shopping district have, for the most part, agreed to the rebuilding proposal, and my work has come to an end, for the time being. With the way things are, this isn't so bad.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Life must go on.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Strange...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I haven't seen a single sheep on my way here...

steps.name: Gentle Creature
steps.text: We have to go now.

steps.name: Solemn Creature
steps.text: Yes. It's time.
The streets today seem awfully quiet.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Was it all... just a dream?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: No... That letter... the rock, and the surfboard that flew right into the sky... They were all real...

Adele tries her hardest to think back on what proof she had that all the adventures she had the past few days were real, but the harder she digs into her memories, the less believable her memories become.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly—

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Are you there?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly—

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Are you still there—
The girl's voice is carried away by the wind.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Your blood-crystal density is fluctuating a little, but for the most part, it's still within the normal range...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You said you pass out suddenly. What do you mean by that, more specifically?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Dr. Ceylon, can Oripathy... cause hallucinations?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Theoretically, it's possible... What did you see?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Lots of Little Black Sheep, and they all talk to me...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: And... I don't know why, but it feels just like I've seen them before...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Well... That sounds like it could've been caused by stress.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But it's weird... Some old miners have told me about similar hallucinations when they came in for consultations...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Let's keep an eye out for a few more days. During that time, make sure you take your medicine on time and get as much rest as you can. If you get any hallucinations again or feel unwell, come to me immediately.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: *sigh*... If only all my patients would be as cooperative as Eyjafjalla, things would be so much easier for me as a doctor. Not like a certain someone here who's always giving me a headache.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Stop chewing me out. I'm here for my follow-up and my medicine, am I not?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Alright, this counts as an improvement. As a way to encourage you, I won't charge you for this consultation.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But I have something I want to ask you.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: A few days ago, I found this basket of obsidian on the shopping district. None of the shops nearby admitted that it was theirs. Do you have any clues about its origins?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Judging from their color, these obsidians are very similar to the one you gave me before... It could very well have been mined around the same time from the volcano.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It wasn't me! I promise! I haven't been near the volcano since I got infected!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: So you mean there are still people mining obsidian illegally.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Enis, what else do you know?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Well... I guess I'd be lying if I said I didn't know anything about it...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Don't try to fudge your way out of this. Out with it!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Dr. Ceylon, some of the workers here know you're the mayor's daughter. It was hard enough to get them to come to you for consultations. If you dig into who's mining obsidian...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: True, what they're doing's not right, but this might just be... a conflict of interest...?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'm me, and the mayor's the mayor. Why must I be grouped together with him?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I came back here this time because I wanted to do something for Siesta with my knowledge. The Rhodes Island office is my blood, sweat, and tears. He's got nothing to do with it!

spans.text: I came back here this time because I wanted to do something for Siesta with my knowledge. The Rhodes Island office is
blood, sweat, and tears. He's got nothing to do with it!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: (It seems like Dr. Ceylon really doesn't like Mayor Herman...)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Maybe Ceylon isn't on very good terms with her father?)

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Anyway, Enis, you know who the obsidian belongs to, right? Take me to them.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It makes me feel kind of like I'm selling them out, but if it's for the greater good...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: A-Alright...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Take me with you. I can help identify obsidian!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: No can do. Last time, you almost sneaked away. You aren't leaving here until you get enough rest.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Huh? What about me...?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'll take you out to eat!
After the night has shrouded the street, Adele steps outside the office.
A lone Little Black Sheep stands outside, staring blankly at the closed door.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Huh? Another hallucination?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What's going on? Didn't I just get some rest...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: *sigh*...
Adele goes around the Little Black Sheep and prepares to go back home.
The Little Black Sheep staggers a little and turns around from the office's door. It sways its head and turns on the miner's lamp on its back. The lamp shines and illuminates the path before Adele.
Adele takes a step forward, and steps onto the shadow cast by the lamp on the Sheep's back.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: There's really a light...?
She turns around and hesitantly reaches her hand out and probes. Then, she feels some warm, fluffy wool.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Not a hallucination?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: No, I've seen you before. You're the sheep who ate the address off the letter. What's that you're carrying on your back... A miner's lamp?
